name: @concordvoice/admin
//engines: node's floor was raised from the former 24.x by the jsdom 30 bump: jsdom@30 declares node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0, so a plain 24.x advertised 24.0-24.14 as supported while the test environment was not. Advisory only — no .npmrc in this repo sets engine-strict — and CI is unaffected either way because setup-node's `node-version: 24` resolves the newest 24.x. The floor form is deliberate over ^24.15.0: it keeps Node 26 valid, which jsdom supports and which developers here actually run.
//overrides_security: brace-expansion@^5.0.9 closes GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (unbounded expansion -> OOM crash, first patched in 5.0.8 on the 5.x line; 2.x at 2.1.3) and GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation; first patched in 5.0.9 on the 5.x line; 2.x at 2.1.4); both transitive via eslint->minimatch. nanoid@^3.3.17 closes GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (custom generators loop indefinitely when size is zero; transitive via vite->postcss). undici has NO override here any more. jsdom is its ONLY consumer in this workspace. jsdom 30.1.3 declares undici ^8.12.1, and that range DOES admit vulnerable versions: eight undici advisories are first patched at 8.12.2 (GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx, GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685, GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26, GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6, GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6, GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472, GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm, GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c), and the 2026-11-18 CVEs cover versions through 8.12.3. The 8.x floor for GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272 is 8.9.0. The lockfile resolves 8.12.4, and the npm-audit gate is the control that blocks a regression; no pin is needed while the lockfile stays there. The former undici@^7.29.0 entry closed that advisory on the 7.x line back when jsdom@29 declared ^7.25.0; against jsdom@30 the SAME entry forces a full major below what jsdom declares, which is why it is removed rather than retargeted. Note this is NOT the fast-uri case described below and does not license sweeping dormant entries: fast-uri was removed because it bound NOTHING, whereas undici binds jsdom's copy and the binding itself became the harm. Verify before reinstating: `npm ls undici --all` for the real consumer set, plus the per-line first_patched of EVERY undici advisory (`gh api /advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=undici`), not just one. minimatch@^11.0.3 closes GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (denial of service through globparts amplification; affects >= 7.0.0 < 11.0.1), dev-only through eslint, @eslint/config-array and @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree. It REPLACES the former ^10.2.6 pin, which is now vulnerable, and its ^11.0.3 floor matches the one services/media-plane already uses. All three consumers declare ^10.2.x (^10.2.6 from eslint, ^10.2.4 from @eslint/config-array, ^10.2.2 from typescript-estree), so this is an intentional upward major skew with three rows in .override-range-baseline.json. A global pin is safe here: this tree resolves a single minimatch, with no 3.x copy and no glob@7 (root uses a scoped pin, because it held both until the SARIF formatter's eslint 8 copy was removed) (docs/ci/minimatch-advisory-repair.md covers both trees). minimatch 11 declares brace-expansion ^5.0.12, satisfied by the pin below. Upstream has shipped the fix: eslint 10.15.0 declares ^11.0.5 and pulls @eslint/config-array 0.23.6 (also ^11.0.5), and @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree 8.73.0 (via typescript-eslint 8.73.0) declares ^11.0.1, all inside the ranges this tree declares. They are not adopted yet because they are inside the 7-day release-age cooldown in .github/dependabot.yml: eslint 10.15.0 clears it on 2026-11-20 and typescript-eslint 8.73.0 on 2026-11-23. Once this lockfile resolves those versions and the override-range lint and npm audit pass without it, drop this pin and its three baseline rows. Never pin minimatch below 11.0.1 again; the older 9.x cap is what once made brace-expansion@5 unreachable here. A former fast-uri override was removed here: this lockfile does not resolve fast-uri, so it bound nothing, and the npm-audit gate — which resolves live against this lockfile on every CI run — is the control that would catch a reintroduction. That was decided for fast-uri specifically, because its motivating advisory is closed AND it bound nothing. It is NOT a general instruction to prune: tar, @tootallnate/once, tmp, serialize-javascript, rollup and ws are dormant in this workspace too, predate this change, and were deliberately left alone rather than swept. RAISED 2026-09-30 to brace-expansion@^5.0.12, because three newer advisories on the 4.x/5.x line sit above 5.0.9: GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p (HIGH, uncontrolled recursion in parseCommaParts, first patched 5.0.10), GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7 (HIGH, uncontrolled recursion on nested brace groups, first patched 5.0.11) and GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr (moderate, quadratic-time expansion of the {a},b} rewrite, first patched 5.0.12). 5.0.12 is the newest release and again sits exactly on the newest floor, with zero headroom. Every consumer was minimatch 10.x declaring ^5.0.x, so the raise stayed on the declared major and added no override-range skew; minimatch 11 declares ^5.0.12.
